recipes.name: Squash Relish
ingredients_raw: 6 (1 pint) canning jars with lids and rings

steps.text: Place squash, onion, and bell peppers in a large bowl; sprinkle with salt and toss to coat. Set aside to drain for 1 hour. Discard liquid.

Place sugar, vinegar, celery seeds, and mustard seeds in a large pot; bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring to dissolve sugar. Stir in squash mixture and return to a boil; cook until vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Inspect 6 pint-sized jars for cracks and rings for rust, discarding any defective ones. Immerse in simmering water until relish is ready. Wash new, unused lids and rings in warm soapy water.

Pack relish into hot, sterilized jars, filling to within ¼-inch of tops. Run a clean knife or thin spatula around insides of jars to remove any air bubbles. Wipe rims with a moist paper towel to remove any residue. Top with lids and screw rings on tightly.

Place a rack in the bottom of a large stockpot and fill halfway with water. Bring to a boil and lower jars 2 inches apart into the boiling water using a holder. Pour in more boiling water to cover jars by at least 1 inch. Bring to a rolling boil, cover, and process for 10 minutes, or the time recommended for your location.

Remove the jars from the stockpot; place onto a cloth-covered or wood surface, several inches apart, until cool. Press centers of lids with a finger to ensure lids do not move up or down. Store in a cool, dark area.

raw_recipe.headline: Squash Relish
raw_recipe.description: This squash relish recipe is made with yellow summer squash and bell peppers in a sweet-tangy pickling liquid for a colorful, refreshing condiment.

review.reviewBody: My mother used to make this relish every summer. It is a wonderful relish that goes well on a southern table. She always sliced her squash and onions in rings though, not diced them. They are much prettier in rings rather than diced.

Thank you for this recipe! I made this years ago, but lost my recipe. I think this is really close. I added a little turmeric and ginger. I grated the squash and used 10 cups instead of the 8 that the recipe called for. It made 12 half pints exactly.

I made 2 batches of this, and on both I only cooked the veggies about 8 minutes to keep a little bit of firmer texture. I made the first batch exactly as written. It was really really good, but a bit too sweet for my taste and not enough kick. 2nd batch I added 3 diced jalepenos, 2 diced cayenne, bumped up the mustard seed to 2 TBS, added a pinch salt, and reduced the sugar to 2 cups. I liked the 2nd batch better, but I think that is all a matter of taste. Wonderful recipe!

Made this recipe last year to use as a Christmas present. However once I tasted it we ate it all. This year I’m making four times as much. The only change I made is that I cold pack my vegetables into the jars then pour my brine on top. This keeps the vegetables crisper. We have served this as a side dish both cold and hot and both are excellent.

I was looking for my old family recipe, and found this one which is so similar it might as well have come from my great aunt. I skipped the step on adding salt to sweat out the water from the veges. I'm on a low, low, low salt diet, and you really don't need to do that step. It canned up so pretty and smells great. I added fennel seeds to the spices.

Good relish! A little sweet, but goes well with salty foods like brats. I made a few minor adjustments. I didn't have any red peppers, so used some yellow ones. I coarsely chopped the vegetables and put them in the food processor to make like relish consistency. I added 2 jalapenos and put the relish in 1/2 pint jars and processed for 5 minutes. Thanks for the recipe!

This is now my favourite use of Patty Pans. Fabulous recipe, I'm now willing a few more fruit before the end of the season so I can stock up for the year! I reduced the sugar by 1/3 like someone else suggested and blitzed in a good processor for a more relish sized spread!

Made my first batch last night! Missing and substituting a few ingredients; I only used 1/2 of a green bell pepper( that's all I found in the fridge, I was completely out of Red Bell peppers so I found a small jar of diced pimentos (Hey they're sweet red bell peppers so it has to work!) I also had yellow squash as the recipe called for, but I also added Yellow Zucchini from my garden! I also misread the recipe directions( I read it no less than 5 times) at the beginning so my veggie mix sat stewing in their own waters and salt for one whole hour! I then saw my mistake and used a sieve to press out most of the water at the end of the hour, lol
It still came out delish! WOW this was a real easy recipe~!~

This is a family favorite! To save time I throw the veggies into the food processer and pulse/chop until they are fairly finely chopped. My recipe calls for turmeric, and I leave out the mustard seed entirely. It's nice as a side as well as a relish!

This is SO good! I had a giant cucuzza squash that I needed to use up, and found out that people often use them interchangeably with summer squash. I decided to try this recipe, but halved it to see if I liked it first. We LOVED it, and I will probably make more asap!
I used a small amount of zucchini because I was short of yellow squash. I also had a few very small green tomatoes so I diced those and included them as well.
I normally dont eat relish but this one is delicious, try it over pork chops.
It's a great recipe but I personally like it better when the veggies are shredded. It's got a sweeter ,delicious taste to it. Excellent!
I used zucchini instead of yellow squash. I LOVE this chow chow! I hand chop the vegetables so it's a little chunky. It's great on peas and beans and we enjoy it on hamburgers, hotdogs, brats.
Absolutely love this added Jalapeños to mine
Have made this for several years and really enjoy it during the winter with Purple Hull peac, White beans and ham hock and on Grilled hot dogs. You won't be disappointed with the results.

I canned over 100 pints of this, my mother in law even had me swap out the yellow squash for zucchini and make 24 of those. They weren't quite as good as the squashbut still very good. Anytime I had to bring out a jar for a meal, it didn't last. I have already got requests for this year when I start canning
Just made this, very excited to try them in a few weeks
This is soooo good! I cut back on the sugar, and it was still very sweet! I will definitely be making more of this!
I've made this recipe twice, once in pint jars and then in half pint jars. We really enjoy the taste! I'm planning to share some jars as gifts.
